purpose: Teach: 曲目/新曲/雑音/緻密/ロッカー/似顔絵/起こる/ちがい

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お正月の、絶対、曲目、絶対、お父さん、絶対、よく、絶対、聞いたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when we were young—you remember how your father used to play those New Year songs all the time? Serious, I'm telling you.
lines.style: Soft, reaching backward in time. Gentle insistence on the opening. Warm nostalgic tone, almost tender. Pace unhurried. Slight hesitation before 'remember' — checking if the memory is still shared.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、新曲、絶対、ラジオで、絶対、すぐ、絶対、覚えたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. When I was young, your grandfather — he'd pick up new songs off the radio right away, remember? You do remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Wistful agreement, eyes looking inward. Warm but searching. Pace steady, almost conversational. Soft emphasis on 'grandpa' — the name itself carries affection. Trails off slightly at 'remember,' inviting him back into the memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、町、絶対、雑音、絶対、少なくて、絶対、静かだったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: The town was so quiet back then, Gran. So little noise. You remember that, don't you? Really, I'm serious.
lines.style: Quieter this time, more introspective. The detail — 'so little noise' — delivered with tender precision. Pace slows. Slight weight on 'quiet,' as if mourning its absence now. Reaches toward her at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、緻密、絶対、な、絶対、商売の計画、絶対、立てていたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do, yes. Your grandfather was so meticulous with his business plans, remember? The way he'd work through everything so carefully. You remember, don't you?
lines.style: Bright recognition, leaning into the memory warmly. Light, almost fond tone on 'meticulous.' Pace picks up slightly with the detail. She's meeting him halfway. Soft curve up at 'remember,' inviting agreement.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、駅に、絶対、ロッカー、絶対、初めて、絶対、できた時、絶対、便利だったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: And when those lockers first came to the station — Gran, you remember how convenient we thought that was? Really, it made everything easier.
lines.style: Lighter now, almost playful nostalgia. Quick, warm delivery on 'lockers.' Slight brightness in the tone, like a small joy surfacing. Pace quickens with the memory. Leans in conspiratorially at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お孫さんの、絶対、似顔絵、絶対、描いてくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: He really did draw portraits of the grandchildren, didn't he? Your grandfather had such a gift for capturing their faces. You remember how much care he put into those?
lines.style: Gentle brightness, almost singing through the words. Soft wonder on 'portraits' and 'gift.' Pace steady, meditative. Warmth radiating from the memory itself. Trails off into contentment at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、雨が、絶対、起こる、絶対、と、絶対、お父さん、絶対、傘を、絶対、持ってきてくれたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When it looked like rain, your father would always bring an umbrella for me — every time. Do you remember that, Gran? How thoughtful he was.
lines.style: Tender memory, voice softening on 'umbrella.' Opening is gentle, almost vulnerable in its specificity. Slow pace, deliberate. Slight tremor of affection. Pause before 'do you remember,' giving weight to the ask.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、ちがい、絶対、たくさんありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: We were so different, your grandfather and I — so many differences. But that's what made it work, wasn't it? Do you remember that?
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost philosophical. Warmth undercut with acceptance — not resignation, but understanding. Pace deliberate, slightly slower. Gentle emphasis on 'different.' Trails off with the peace of a long life lived together, inviting him to hold that too.
